newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU has potential for large wheat sale to Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: EU has potential for large wheat sale to Bulgaria.

text.p: The European Union, which harvested a record grain crop in 1996, has the potential to sell Bulgaria between 200,000 and 300,000 tonnes of soft wheat in the current 1996/97 season, EU grain sources said on Monday.
But they did not say if a particular deal was in the pipeline nor how Bulgaria would pay for the wheat.
The latest data from EU grain trade lobby Coceral put the EU grain crop at 203.1 million tonnes, of which 91 million tonnes was soft wheat.
Bulgaria is suffering from a grain shortage after uncontrolled exports two years ago and a poor harvest last year depleted supplies.

Bulgaria, which needs 450,000 tonnes of wheat to fill the gap until the new crop, has reached a deal with Argentina for 130,000 tonnes of grain, Deputy Agriculture Minister Alexander Rangelov said last month.
It is also negotiating an agreement under the USDA's GSM 102 export credit guarantee program for 130,000-150,000 tonnes from the US.
A European Union delegation headed by EU external relations commissioner Hans van den Broek is expected in Bulgaria on March 17-18 to discuss EU grain aid worth about two million Ecus.
The EU mission takes place as Bulgaria is about to reach an agreement on a funding program with the IMF to help stabilise its ailing economy.
But exporters said the EU aid, if granted, was not sufficient to fund exports of 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes of wheat to Bulgaria.
